**My pick is the Anker Nano Power Bank (5K) for most people. If you want the thinnest one, get the Baseus Picogo Air.** I'm going by the Android Central and 9to5Mac roundups and Anker's product page. I haven't tested any of these myself.

**Best overall slim: Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo)**
- It's 0.34" thick and weighs 122 g (4.3 oz), with 5,000mAh and 15W Qi2 wireless charging. Anker says it's tuned for the iPhone 17 series. ([Anker](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank))
- 9to5Mac's reviewer has used it and says it feels premium and runs cooler than the competition. He calls it the closest alternative to Apple's own MagSafe battery. ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/))
- It costs $54.99 and comes in several colors. [Buy at Anker](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank).
- Anker says cases thicker than 2.5 mm weaken the magnetic connection. Check your case.

**Thinnest and lightest: Baseus Picogo Air AM71 (5,000mAh)**
- Android Central calls it the thinnest and lightest of the slim Qi2 banks it tested, at 0.27" and 104 g. ([Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge))
- Wireless charging is only 7.5W, slower than the Anker's 15W. Wired output is 22.5W.
- It has no battery display, but you can check the charge by tapping it to your phone and opening the app.
- It costs $69.99 to $79.99 depending on color, and the review says it goes on sale often. [Buy at Amazon](https://target.georiot.com/Proxy.ashx?tsid=169923&GR_URL=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2Fdp%2FB0GWPP9Q26%3Ftag%3Dftr-androidcentral-us-20%26linkCode%3Dogi%26th%3D1%26psc%3D1%26ascsubtag%3Dac-us-2449070638521009969).

**Slim with solid-state battery: ReelCharge ReelSafe (5,000mAh)**
- It's 0.35" thick and weighs 119 g, with 15W Qi2 wireless and 20W wired charging. It uses a semi-solid-state battery and has an LED display.
- It costs $49.50. [Buy at Amazon](https://target.georiot.com/Proxy.ashx?tsid=169923&GR_URL=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2Fdp%2FB0H34PD1WM%3Ftag%3Dftr-androidcentral-us-20%26linkCode%3Dogi%26th%3D1%26psc%3D1%26ascsubtag%3Dac-us-2449070638521009969).
- ReelCharge is a little-known brand, so I'd go with Anker unless the price or the battery type matters to you.

**If you want more capacity and can accept a thicker bank**
- **INIU SnapGo Air (10,000mAh):** It does 25W Qi2.2 wireless and 45W wired charging, and it includes a built-in lanyard-style cable. It's 0.5" thick and 195 g, and costs about $43. [Buy at Amazon](https://target.georiot.com/Proxy.ashx?tsid=169923&GR_URL=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2Fdp%2FB0H448SDMB%3Ftag%3Dftr-androidcentral-us-20%26linkCode%3Dogi%26th%3D1%26psc%3D1%26ascsubtag%3Dac-us-2449070638521009969).
- **TORRAS MiniMag Pro (10,000mAh):** It's IP54 dust and water resistant, 0.57" thick, and 195 g. It costs $69.99 to $89.99 depending on color. [Buy at Amazon](https://target.georiot.com/Proxy.ashx?tsid=169923&GR_URL=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2Fdp%2FB0H6WSLM2B%3Ftag%3Dftr-androidcentral-us-20%26linkCode%3Dogi%26th%3D1%26psc%3D1%26ascsubtag%3Dac-us-2449070638521009969).

**Which to choose**
- A 5,000mAh bank won't fully recharge an iPhone 17. Anker itself says you'll get roughly 2,750 to 3,500mAh of usable power.
- For a top-up in a pocket, get the Anker, or the Baseus if thickness matters most.
- For a full recharge or more, get the INIU.
- The 9to5Mac roundup also lists a Baseus bank for $24.99 that doesn't support Qi2. It's limited to 7.5W wireless, so I'd skip it.
